tasks.title: Task 1
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: If inflation rises, the central bank raises the policy rate.
If the board approves the budget, the firm will hire three analysts next month.
If demand increases, the warehouse will restocks overnight.
If cash flow improves, payroll will processes on Friday.
If the client signs today, logistics would ship the sample kit tomorrow for certain.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — This is a clean zero conditional: present simple in both clauses for a general business rule that always holds when the condition is met.

Tip: For habits and policy rules, keep both sides in present simple — not will.

TRUE — First conditional: a real future possibility takes present simple in the if-clause and will + base verb in the result.

Tip: After if for a real future plan, use present simple, then will in the main clause.

FALSE — The result clause mixes will with a third-person -s form ("will restocks"). After will you need the base form restock.

Tip: Modal will always takes a bare infinitive: will restock, never will restocks.

FALSE — After will the verb must stay bare: will process, not will processes. Agreement -s never follows a modal.

Tip: Scan will + verb: if you see an -s on that verb, the line is broken.

FALSE — A real tomorrow delivery plan needs will ship, not would ship. Would belongs to unreal or polite second-conditional territory.

Tip: Open near-term plans → will; reserve would for unreal or soft hypothetical results.
tasks.solution_overview: Walk each sentence like a checklist: is this a general rule (zero) or a real future plan (first)? Zero keeps present + present; first keeps present + will. Three lines fail on form — will + -s, and would where will is required.

tasks.title: Task 2
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: If the start-up had more working capital, it would expand into two new regions.
If I were the finance director, I would postpone the share buy-back.
If the supplier would have confirmed earlier, we would have met the launch date.
If margins were higher, the retailer would stock premium SKUs.
If the auditor were available on Monday, we would close the ledger then.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Second conditional: past simple in the if-clause plus would + base verb for an unreal present or future business scenario.

Tip: Unreal now/soon → if + past simple, main clause would + infinitive.

TRUE — Formal were is the preferred subjunctive after if I for unreal advice or role-play, paired with would in the result.

Tip: In exams, prefer If I were … would … over If I was for hypothetical roles.

FALSE — Classic trap: do not put would have in the if-clause. The unreal past condition needs past perfect: If the supplier had confirmed earlier…

Tip: Never write if … would have; use if … had + past participle instead.

TRUE — Standard second conditional for a counterfactual present about margins and assortment.

Tip: Past simple + would is the default unreal-present frame.

TRUE — Were with a third-person singular subject is fine in careful business English for an unreal present condition.

Tip: If X were … would … is exam-safe for unreal present, even with he/she/it.
tasks.solution_overview: These lines test unreal present (second conditional) and the infamous if … would have trap. Keep would only in the result clause; the if-clause wants past simple or were, never would have.

tasks.title: Task 3
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: If the bank had tightened covenants sooner, the borrower would have refinanced elsewhere.
Had the logistics team booked the slots, the shipment would have cleared customs on time.
Had the CFO hedged the exposure, the firm will avoid the currency loss.
If procurement had dual-sourced the chip, production would not have stalled.
Had marketing tested the creative, the campaign would have launched with fewer revisions.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Third conditional: past perfect in the if-clause and would have + past participle for a closed past outcome.

Tip: Past unreal → if + had + V3, main clause would have + V3.

TRUE — Inverted third conditional: Had + subject + past participle replaces If + subject + had, with the same would have result.

Tip: Had the team … would have … equals If the team had … would have …

FALSE — After inverted Had … the result must stay in the third-conditional world (would have), not will. Will clashes with a finished past condition.

Tip: Inversion still needs would have / could have / might have — never bare will.

TRUE — Classic third conditional on a missed sourcing decision and its past production impact.

Tip: Check both verbs: had dual-sourced + would not have stalled.

TRUE — Another clean Had-inversion third conditional about campaign testing.

Tip: If the sentence starts with Had + past participle phrase, expect would have in the main clause.
tasks.solution_overview: Focus on closed past regrets: past perfect (or Had-inversion) plus would have. The broken line swaps will into a past counterfactual — that tense clash is the giveaway.

tasks.title: Task 4
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: If the firm had entered the Nordic market last year, it would have a stronger brand there now.
If inventory were lower today, we would have ordered less last quarter.
If the tender is won, the contractor will mobilise within ten days.
If energy prices fall, factories cut night-shift overtime.
If I would be the project lead, I would freeze scope changes.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Mixed conditional: past cause (had entered) with a present result (would have a stronger brand now).

Tip: Past cause → present result: if + past perfect, would + present-state verb.

TRUE — The other common mix: unreal present condition (were lower today) explaining a different past action (would have ordered).

Tip: Present unreal → past result: if + past simple/were, would have + V3.

TRUE — Straightforward first conditional for a still-open tender outcome.

Tip: Open future deal → present + will.

TRUE — Zero conditional describing how plants generally respond when energy prices fall.

Tip: General operations rule → present + present.

FALSE — Avoid would in the if-clause. For an unreal role use If I were the project lead, I would freeze…

Tip: If I would be is almost always wrong; rewrite as If I were / If I was (informal).
tasks.solution_overview: Four lines are healthy mixes of zero, first, and mixed conditionals. Isolate the if-clause that wrongly uses would — that is the only hard fail on this card.

tasks.title: Task 5
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: Unless the invoice is paid by Friday, the wholesaler will suspend further deliveries.
If the KPI dashboard updates nightly, managers review exceptions each morning.
If headcount rose next spring, HR will open a graduate scheme.
Provided that compliance clears the script, the webinar will go live at noon.
If liquidity dried up tomorrow, treasurers would draw the revolving facility.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Unless + present simple works like a first-conditional if-not clause, with will in the result.

Tip: Unless ≈ if not; keep present after unless for real future threats.

TRUE — Zero conditional for a recurring overnight data habit and the morning review that follows.

Tip: Habitual systems → present in both clauses.

FALSE — Mixing past simple (rose) with will for a still-possible next-spring plan is inconsistent. Use rises … will open, or rose … would open for unreal.

Tip: Match time frames: real future needs present + will, not past + will.

TRUE — Provided that behaves like if in a first conditional and correctly pairs with will.

Tip: Provided that / as long as take the same tense pattern as if.

TRUE — Second conditional for an unlikely near-term liquidity crunch: past simple + would.

Tip: Unlikely tomorrow-stress → past + would.
tasks.solution_overview: Watch connectors (unless, provided that) — they follow the same tense rules as if. The weak sentence pairs a past-form condition with will for an open future plan.

tasks.title: Task 6
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: If the joint venture had secured the licence in March, it would be operating at full capacity now.
Had interest rates stayed low, the REIT would refinance the portfolio last autumn.
If customers complained about packaging, the brand redesigns the inserts.
If I were advising the board, I would ring-fence the contingency reserve.
If the merger would have closed in Q2, synergies would have appeared sooner.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Mixed: past perfect condition with a present continuous-style result (would be operating now).

Tip: Past decision → present state: had + V3, then would + be + -ing / would + base.

FALSE — Had … stayed sets a third/mixed past frame, but would refinance (simple) fails to mark the missed autumn action; need would have refinanced.

Tip: A finished past result after Had … needs would have + V3.

TRUE — Zero conditional for a standing customer-service rule.

Tip: Whenever-style complaints → present + present.

TRUE — If I were + would is the polished second-conditional advisory pattern.

Tip: Hypothetical advice voice: If I were …, I would …

FALSE — Another if … would have trap in the condition clause; rewrite as If the merger had closed in Q2…

Tip: Delete would from every if-clause; use had + V3 for past unreal.
tasks.solution_overview: Two failures hide in past counterfactuals: one under-marks the result (would instead of would have), and one illegally places would have after if. The true lines show clean zero, mixed, and If I were patterns.

tasks.title: Task 7
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: Should the underwriter demand more disclosure, the issuer will file an amended prospectus.
If unit costs fall below target, the plant will increase daily throughput.
If the franchisee paid royalties on time, the brand renews the territory next year.
Had the warehouse installed scanners earlier, picking errors would have dropped.
If demand softens, dynamic pricing lowers weekend rates automatically.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Formal first-conditional inversion with Should + subject + base verb, then will in the result.

Tip: Should the X … will … = If the X … will … for real future contingencies.

TRUE — Ordinary first conditional on a cost-threshold trigger.

Tip: Present after if + will for operational targets.

FALSE — Past simple paid paired with present renews for a next-year plan is a tense mash-up. Use pays … will renew, or paid … would renew.

Tip: Do not mix a past if-clause with a present-simple future result.

TRUE — Had-inversion third conditional on a past technology investment.

Tip: Had + V3 … would have + V3 is the inversion checklist.

TRUE — Zero conditional for an automated pricing rule.

Tip: System rules that always fire → present + present.
tasks.solution_overview: Should-inversion is just a formal first conditional — keep will in the result. Reject any line that jumps from a past if-clause straight into a present-simple future promise.

tasks.title: Task 8
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: If the catalogue were printed in colour, retail buyers would place larger orders.
If the courier arrives before noon, the clinic will still process same-day claims.
If R&D had patented the coating, competitors would not copy it so easily now.
If we would receive the escrow release, we will settle the contractors.
Were the exchange rate more stable, exporters would quote longer fixed prices.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Second conditional with were for an unreal present product decision.

Tip: Were / past simple + would marks counterfactual present.

TRUE — First conditional for a real same-day operations window.

Tip: Present + will for open daytime logistics.

TRUE — Mixed: past perfect cause with a present result (would not copy … now).

Tip: Past IP choice → present competitive pain: had + V3, would + base.

FALSE — Double fault: would in the if-clause and will in the result for what should be a simple first conditional (If we receive … we will settle).

Tip: Strip would from if; use present + will for real receipts.

TRUE — Were-inversion second conditional (Were the exchange rate …) equals If the exchange rate were…

Tip: Were + noun phrase … would … is formal unreal present.
tasks.solution_overview: Healthy second, first, mixed, and Were-inversion lines surround one toxic if we would receive … will settle pair. Train your eye to delete would from every if-clause first.

tasks.title: Task 9
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: If the bond had been rated investment-grade, pension funds would hold larger positions today.
If churn stays under two percent, the SaaS firm will beat its ARR guidance.
Had the pilot failed safety checks, regulators would suspend the route indefinitely.
If staffing were flexible, overtime premiums would fall during peak weeks.
If the auctioneer would have set a higher reserve, the lot would have sold for more.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Mixed conditional: past rating event → present portfolio behaviour (would hold … today).

Tip: Look for now/today after a had-been condition — that signals mixed, not pure third.

TRUE — First conditional on a live KPI threshold and forward guidance.

Tip: Open metric path → present + will.

FALSE — Had the pilot failed frames a closed past check, so the result needs would have suspended, not would suspend (which reads like a present/future habit).

Tip: Past inversion + ongoing would is usually wrong; prefer would have for finished past results.

TRUE — Second conditional about an unreal present HR policy.

Tip: Were + would for counterfactual workforce design.

FALSE — If … would have set is the prohibited pattern; use If the auctioneer had set a higher reserve…

Tip: Past unreal conditions: had + V3 only — never would have after if.
tasks.solution_overview: Distinguish mixed present results from pure third-conditional past results. Two lines fail: one under-marks a past result after Had…, and one still smuggles would have into the if-clause.

tasks.title: Task 10
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: As long as collateral covers the drawdown, the facility will remain available.
If freight rates spiked last winter, importers would switch to rail now.
If the prototype passes EMC tests, manufacturing will tool the moulds.
If I was the risk officer yesterday, I would have blocked the trade.
If volatility increases, option premiums rise across the board.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — As long as + present simple with will is a standard first-conditional credit condition.

Tip: As long as / so long as follow first-conditional tense logic.

FALSE — A finished last-winter spike needs past perfect (had spiked) for a mixed link to now, or a different framing. Past simple + would … now is not the clean mixed pattern.

Tip: Past cause of a present result → if + had + V3, would + present.

TRUE — First conditional for a gated manufacturing step still ahead.

Tip: Open test gate → present + will.

FALSE — Yesterday forces a past unreal: If I had been the risk officer yesterday, I would have blocked… Was + would have mismatches the time adverb.

Tip: With yesterday/last week, prefer had been … would have, not was … would have.

TRUE — Zero conditional market rule: higher volatility, higher premiums.

Tip: Market identities → present + present.
tasks.solution_overview: Time adverbs are the tell. Last winter and yesterday demand past-perfect conditions for counterfactuals; as long as and open tests stay in first-conditional territory.

tasks.title: Task 11
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: Had tariffs been announced sooner, sourcing teams would already be dual-qualified now.
If the retailer offers free returns, conversion rates climb in the app.
If cash reserves are thinner, the group would cancel the dividend next week.
If the engineer had calibrated the line, scrap rates would be lower this morning.
Were investors fully informed, they would tolerate a longer payback period.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Mixed after Had-inversion: past tariff shock → present continuous-like state (would already be dual-qualified now).

Tip: Had … been + would be … now is a valid mixed inversion.

TRUE — Zero conditional e-commerce rule linking a standing offer to conversion behaviour.

Tip: Standing commercial rules → present + present.

FALSE — Present simple are thinner with would cancel is a second-conditional mismatch; use were thinner … would cancel, or are thinner … will cancel.

Tip: Present real → will; unreal present → past/were + would — do not cross-wire them.

TRUE — Mixed: past calibration failure/success with a present scrap-rate result this morning.

Tip: Had + V3 … would be … now/this morning = mixed.

TRUE — Were-inversion second conditional on investor psychology.

Tip: Were + subject complement … would … for unreal present.
tasks.solution_overview: Real present facts take will; unreal present takes were/past + would. The false line keeps a real-present verb (are) but slips into would for next week.

tasks.title: Task 12
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: If the consortium bids aggressively, the city will award the concession this quarter.
If wage growth outpaced productivity last year, unit labour costs would be elevated now.
If the broker would confirm the allocation, traders will hedge by the open.
If downtime exceeds four hours, service-level credits apply automatically.
Had the insurer priced flood risk correctly, claims would not have wiped the book.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — First conditional for a live tender still in play.

Tip: Open award window → present + will.

FALSE — Last year as a factual past driver of a present state needs had outpaced, not outpaced alone, in careful mixed form: If wage growth had outpaced … would be elevated now.

Tip: For past→present mixed, upgrade the if-clause to past perfect.

FALSE — Would confirm after if plus will hedge is a first-conditional wreck; write If the broker confirms … traders will hedge…

Tip: Real pre-open plans never put would in the if-clause.

TRUE — Zero conditional SLA rule written into the contract language.

Tip: Automatic contractual consequences → present + present.

TRUE — Full third conditional on a closed underwriting mistake.

Tip: Had + V3 … would not have + V3 for finished past damage.
tasks.solution_overview: Two traps: a mixed that forgot past perfect after last year, and a first conditional polluted with would. The clean lines stay strictly first, zero, or third.

tasks.title: Task 13
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: If the CFO were to disclose the impairment early, analysts would reassess guidance within hours.
If negotiations break down, counsel will file for interim relief.
Had working capital been ring-fenced, the turnaround plan would succeed last month.
If order books thin further, factories will idle weekend shifts.
If I would have chaired the audit committee, related-party deals would have faced harder questions.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Were to + infinitive is an accepted formal second-conditional variant for a tentative unreal future disclosure.

Tip: If X were to + verb … would … softens an unlikely future step.

TRUE — First conditional litigation contingency still open.

Tip: Present + will for live legal forks.

FALSE — Had … been ring-fenced points to a past closed window (last month), so the result needs would have succeeded, not would succeed.

Tip: Past inversion + last month → would have + V3.

TRUE — First conditional operations response to thinning order books.

Tip: Real deterioration path → present + will.

FALSE — If I would have chaired is the textbook trap; correct: If I had chaired the audit committee…

Tip: Memorise the ban: no would have after if — ever.
tasks.solution_overview: Were to is a polished second-conditional option, not an error. Failures here under-specify a past result after Had… and recycle the if I would have chaired trap.

tasks.title: Task 14
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: Even if the patent lapses, the know-how will still protect margins for a while.
If yields had climbed faster, duration risk would look worse on today's dashboard.
If the stewardess announces a delay, passengers update their onward bookings.
Supposing the lease is extended, the bakery will keep the high-street unit.
If regulators had signalled forbearance, banks would not tighten lending standards so sharply now.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Even if still follows first-conditional tenses for a real possibility that does not block the result.

Tip: Even if + present, will … keeps the same skeleton as if.

TRUE — Mixed: faster past climb in yields → present dashboard appearance (would look … today).

Tip: Had + V3 … would + present verb + today/now = mixed.

TRUE — Zero conditional passenger-behaviour rule at the gate (business-travel operations context).

Tip: Habitual responses → present + present.

TRUE — Supposing that/if-equivalent first conditional with will.

Tip: Supposing ≈ if for real future estate decisions.

TRUE — Mixed policy signal: past forbearance cue → present lending stance.

Tip: Past perfect condition + would + present verb + now.
tasks.solution_overview: All five are sound — a rare full-true card. Confirm even if / supposing keep first-conditional logic, and that both mixed lines genuinely link a past perfect cause to a present result with now/today.

tasks.title: Task 15
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: If the incubator mentors founders weekly, survival rates improve after year one.
If customs had cleared the consignment on Monday, shelves would not be empty this afternoon.
If I were in your position at treasury, I would ladder the maturities.
Had the pitch deck mentioned churn, the VC would ask harder questions in the room.
If spot prices rally, hedgers will roll their contracts forward.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Zero conditional describing an incubator operating model and its usual outcome.

Tip: Programme design rules → present + present.

TRUE — Mixed: Monday clearance (past perfect) versus empty shelves now (would not be … this afternoon).

Tip: Past logistics miss → present stockout: had + V3, would + be.

TRUE — Classic If I were … would … advisory second conditional in a treasury setting.

Tip: Exam gold: If I were …, I would …

FALSE — Had … mentioned sets a past counterfactual about the deck, so the room Q&A that followed needs would have asked, not would ask.

Tip: Finished past meeting → would have + V3 after Had…

TRUE — First conditional markets line for an open rally scenario.

Tip: Live price path → present + will.
tasks.solution_overview: Only the pitch-deck inversion fails by leaving the result in would ask instead of would have asked. Everything else cleanly covers zero, mixed, If I were, and first.

tasks.title: Task 16
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: If carbon prices climb, cement producers pass on surcharges within the quarter.
If the syndicate had allocated more paper to retail, the aftermarket would be firmer today.
If onboarding takes longer than five days, enterprise clients will escalate to the account lead.
If the board would approve a rights issue, dilution would worry existing holders.
Were cash conversion weaker, ratings agencies would flag liquidity metrics.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Zero conditional industry pricing response.

Tip: Sector rule of thumb → present + present.

TRUE — Mixed primary-market decision (had allocated) with today's aftermarket tone (would be firmer today).

Tip: Past allocation → present trading: had + V3, would + be + today.

TRUE — First conditional SLA/escalation path still available.

Tip: Open service risk → present + will.

FALSE — Would approve after if is illegal; for unreal present write If the board approved … would worry, or for real future If the board approves … will worry.

Tip: Kill would in the if-clause, then choose second vs first consistently.

TRUE — Were-inversion second conditional on credit metrics.

Tip: Were + comparative … would … for unreal present credit stress.
tasks.solution_overview: Four lines are textbook. The false one parks would inside the if-clause before another would — double would is your red flag.

tasks.title: Task 17
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: Had the earn-out been structured more tightly, the acquirer would not be litigating the targets now.
If utilisation dips below seventy percent, the airline will wet-lease fewer aircraft next season.
If the controller was to restate revenue, auditors would expand sampling immediately.
If freight forwarders had digitalised documents earlier, demurrage would have been lower last peak season.
Only if collateral is topped up will the lender release the next tranche.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Mixed Had-inversion: past earn-out design → present litigation (would not be litigating … now).

Tip: Had … been + would be + -ing + now = mixed inversion.

TRUE — First conditional fleet-planning response to utilisation.

Tip: Season-ahead ops plan → present + will.

FALSE — Formal tentative unreal prefers were to, not was to, with a singular controller in careful exam English: If the controller were to restate…

Tip: In formal papers, stick to were to (not was to) after if for this pattern.

TRUE — Pure third conditional on a finished peak-season cost outcome.

Tip: Had + V3 … would have been … for closed past peaks.

TRUE — Only if inversion in a first-conditional credit release: Only if … will + subject + verb.

Tip: Only if moves will before the subject — still a real future condition.
tasks.solution_overview: Advanced packaging: mixed Had-inversion, Only if … will inversion, and the were to vs was to formality trap. Only the was to line should fall.

tasks.title: Task 18
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: If goodwill had not been written down, equity ratios would look healthier on the March pack.
If the night shift finishes the batch, QC will sample before dawn.
If distributors stocked deeper inventories, stock-outs would have been rarer during last Black Friday.
If I would be less exposed to FX, I would sleep better before reporting day.
Should volumes recover, the mill will restart the idle kiln.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Mixed accounting counterfactual: past write-down choice → present appearance of March ratios.

Tip: Had not + V3 … would look … on [present pack] = mixed.

TRUE — First conditional plant schedule still open tonight.

Tip: Same-night plan → present + will.

TRUE — Mixed the other way: unreal present stocking policy explaining a different past Black Friday (would have been rarer).

Tip: Present unreal → past result: if + past simple, would have + V3.

FALSE — If I would be is wrong; use If I were less exposed to FX, I would sleep better…

Tip: Replace If I would be with If I were every time.

TRUE — Should-inversion first conditional for a volume recovery path.

Tip: Should volumes … will … = If volumes … will …
tasks.solution_overview: You need both mixed directions here — past→present and present→past — plus Should-inversion. The single fail is If I would be for an unreal present state.

tasks.title: Task 19
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: Were it not for the hedge, the importer would be posting large FX losses this quarter.
If the catalogue had shipped in January, spring sell-through would have peaked earlier.
If headhunters find a match, the CHRO will reopen the search committee.
Had the covenant waiver been granted, the firm will avoid a technical default last Friday.
If payment terms lengthened industry-wide, working-capital cycles would stretch for everyone.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Were it not for … is a formal second/mixed-style inversion meaning if it were not for the hedge, with would be posting now.

Tip: Were it not for X … would … = If it were not for X …

TRUE — Pure third conditional on a missed January catalogue drop.

Tip: Had + V3 … would have + V3 for closed seasonal timing.

TRUE — First conditional hiring contingency.

Tip: Open search branch → present + will.

FALSE — Had … been granted plus last Friday demands would have avoided, not will avoid.

Tip: Past waiver story → would have + V3; will cannot rewrite last Friday.

TRUE — Second conditional industry-wide counterfactual on payment terms.

Tip: Past simple + would for unreal present credit norms.
tasks.solution_overview: Were it not for is advanced but legitimate. The broken Had … will avoid line tries to put a future auxiliary on last Friday — tense suicide.

tasks.title: Task 20
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: If the underwriter would have priced the IPO more tightly, aftermarket volatility would have been lower.
If backlog clears by June, the yard will takes two more hulls.
If energy hedges rolled off already, spot exposure would be biting harder now.
If I would be running the category, I would delist the slowest SKUs before the reset.
Had cyber insurance been renewed on time, incident costs would have been capped.
tactical_explanations:
FALSE — The if-clause must not contain would have; write If the underwriter had priced the IPO more tightly…

Tip: Final reminder: if + had + V3, never if + would have.

FALSE — After will use the base verb take, not takes. Agreement -s never follows will.

Tip: will take / will ship / will hire — never will takes.

FALSE — A finished roll-off that explains present pain needs past perfect: If energy hedges had rolled off already…

Tip: Past cause of a present result → had + V3 in the if-clause.

FALSE — If I would be running is wrong; write If I were running the category, I would delist…

Tip: Replace If I would be with If I were in unreal present advice.

TRUE — Had-inversion third conditional on a missed renewal.

Tip: Had + been + V3 … would have been … seals the past counterfactual.
tasks.solution_overview: Capstone stress test: four traps (if … would have, will + -s, missing past perfect in a mixed, If I would be) and one clean Had-inversion third conditional. Hunt errors before celebrating the true line.
